analysis.investment_thesis: Aadhar Housing Finance is a steady compounder in affordable housing — a segment with durable, policy-backed demand — delivering 16.1% revenue CAGR and 33.4% PAT CAGR over six years. Valuation at 20.8x P/E is at the top of my comfort zone, and I would wait for a better entry price before adding significantly.
key_strengths: Consistent PAT CAGR of 33.4% over 6 years (INR 162 Cr → 912 Cr) with expanding margins — real earnings, not accounting tricks
Promoter holding stable at 64.9% — strong alignment, no stake reduction visible
Serves low-income housing segment with government tailwind (PMAY), creating predictable and sticky demand
key_risks: D/E of 2.55 — high in absolute terms; any credit cycle tightening or rate spike can compress NIMs and stress asset quality
Entirely debt-funded growth model means OCF is structurally negative; business health depends on capital markets staying open
Rising finance costs (INR 732 Cr → 1,174 Cr, 2019–2025) are growing faster than reported but PAT expansion masks spread compression risk
red_flags: Operating cash flow negative every single year — 0/5 positive; normal for HFCs but requires constant external funding
P/B at 3.11x leaves limited margin of safety if credit quality deteriorates
No dividend history visible — earnings quality signal absent for an NBFC of this scale
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aadhar Housing Finance operates in the right segment — affordable home loans in Tier 2/3 India — where demand is durable, competition is fragmented, and government subsidies provide additional cushion. Revenue has grown at 16.1% CAGR and net profit at 33.4% CAGR since 2019, with the equity base doubling to INR 6,894 Cr by 2025 following an IPO. ROE of 16.9% is acceptable but not exceptional for an HFC; I would want to see it stabilise above 18% as scale increases.

For an HFC, D/E of 2.55 is sector-normal and I do not penalise it the way I would an industrial company. However, total borrowings of INR 16,322 Cr against equity of INR 6,894 Cr means any deterioration in asset quality (NPA data unavailable here) could be painful. At 20.8x P/E with a forward P/E of 16.2x, the stock is fairly priced but not cheap enough for me to build a large position — I prefer to buy good businesses at a discount, not at full price.
